title: AI is killing All About Berlin
lede: Nicolas Bouliane, who has made his living from the guide site All About Berlin since 2020, says Google's AI Overviews have taken about three quarters of its traffic.

points: A search now shows ads and an AI answer drawn from his guides before any link to the site itself.
Government offices refer people to the guides, and the site inspired two official portals.
He says other site owners have paywalled their work or stopped updating it.
In the thread, Bouliane says things have got worse since the post and next year may be his last running the site full time.

points.text: Many see a loop that eats itself: AI depends on openly published human work while removing the reason to publish it.
One commenter says many readers simply prefer an AI summary to affiliate-driven pages; a reply notes niche answers still need checking against the sources.
A comparison to ad blocking, which HN usually defends, splits the thread; replies say the difference is that readers never visit the site at all.
Several argue small publishers need a different revenue model, with ad-funded sites already weakened by ad blockers.
